bottleneck: Germline-competent editing, embryo models, and heritable interventions outpace the ethical frameworks meant to govern them: institutional review boards and national regulators were built for drugs, not for edits that propagate through generations. The He Jiankui episode revealed that determined actors can bypass every safeguard, and international norms are advisory, unenforceable, and interpreted differently across cultures. The technology's global availability means the most permissive jurisdiction effectively sets the standard for all.
current_state: Calls for a global observatory or moratorium recur after each controversy, but binding international governance of heritable editing does not exist. Oversight remains national, voluntary, and reactive.

sources.title: A double-edged sword: CRISPR-Cas9 is emerging as a revolutionary technique for genome editing

title: Heritable editing outruns enforceable governance
why_it_blocks: Without credible global guardrails, the field oscillates between reckless experiments and reactionary bans — both of which block responsible progress toward eliminating inherited disease, while public trust erodes with each scandal.
